fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Front Driveway; Open Green Space; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Rocky Terrain; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Rocky Terrain; Long Driveway; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the road entrance to the driveway so responders can locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly on both sides with posts or reflective markers, especially if vegetation narrows the opening.
• Trim trees and shrubs along both sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Maintain vertical clearance along the driveway to at least 14 feet so fire apparatus and ambulances can travel the full length without interference from overhanging branches.
• Identify and designate a turnaround area near the residence so large vehicles are not required to back the full length of the driveway to exit.
• Mark the turnaround area with ground-level reflectors or posts so drivers can locate its boundaries at night or in low visibility.
• Clear vegetation from the edges of the designated turnaround area so a full-size emergency vehicle can complete the turn without going onto unstable or rocky ground.
• Keep the turnaround area free of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials at all times.
• Thin dense vegetation along the sides of the driveway to reduce the risk of fire moving from surrounding vegetation onto the access route.
• Mark any sections of the driveway where rocky terrain creates drop-offs or soft shoulders so responders are aware of edge hazards when pulling over or staging

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Mixed Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Open Terrain; Long Driveway; Single Access Route; Rock Outcrop; Grass Cover; Tree Cluster
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from trees that are close to the house to create separation between the tree canopy and the structure.
• Thin trees in the clusters nearest to the house to reduce the amount of vegetation that could carry fire toward it.
• Cut or mow grass growing close to the house and any outbuildings down to a short height.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or immediately next to the house.
• Thin shrubs scattered across the property to break up continuous patches of vegetation between tree clusters and the house.
• Separate shrubs from nearby trees by clearing vegetation between them so fire cannot move easily from low growth up into tree canopies.
• Keep the area around rock outcrops clear of dead grass and shrubs that can accumulate in cracks and gaps.
• Clear overhanging branches along the full length of the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of fallen branches, accumulated debris, and encroaching vegetation along its edges.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate quickly from the road, particularly if visibility is reduced by smoke.
• Keep a wide, clear turning area near the house so fire trucks can turn around without difficulty given the single access route.
• Remove dead grass, leaves, and other loose debris that collect against the base of the house and any other structures on the property.
